title: Choose success metrics and guardrails
summary: Decide how you will know the work succeeded, and what must not get worse along the way. Clear metrics make every later decision easier.

beginner: Start from the outcome in your problem statement. Ask: what would we see if this worked?
Pick one main metric that shows the outcome, such as task completion, time saved, adoption or retention.
Add one or two supporting metrics that show progress earlier, such as how many people try the new step.
Add one or two guardrail metrics: things that must not get worse, such as support calls, errors, satisfaction or cost.
For each metric, write how it is calculated, where the data comes from and today's baseline.
Set a target and a date, and agree them with your team and sponsor.
intermediate: Define one primary outcome metric with a clear formula and data source.
Record baselines and set targets with dates.
Confirm the data can be collected; if not, add tracking to the plan.
experienced: Link the primary metric to the product's north star and to company goals.
Choose guardrails that protect users, quality and the business, and set thresholds that would stop a launch.
Check that metrics cannot be easily gamed and that they reflect long-term value, not short-term spikes.
Agree how and when results will be reviewed and who decides what happens next.

canDelegateTo.task: Define formulas, find baselines and check the data exists
Confirm what can be tracked and what new tracking is needed

toolExamples.confluence: Add a metrics table to the problem statement page: name, formula, source, baseline, target, date.
toolExamples.amplitude: Save each metric as a chart now, so you can watch the baseline before anything changes.
toolExamples.ga4: Check which events already exist for the journey and list the ones you will need to add.
toolExamples.looker: Define the metrics once in a shared model so every report uses the same definition.
toolExamples.claude: Describe your outcome and ask for candidate metrics and guardrails, then ask how each could be gamed.

definitionOfDone: One primary metric, supporting metrics and guardrails agreed
Formula, data source and baseline recorded for each
pitfalls: Measuring activity, such as features shipped, instead of outcomes
No guardrails, so a win in one place hides harm in another
Choosing metrics you cannot measure yet without planning the tracking
